lessons.why: restart after an end before visual_request-12

turns.teacherReply: Namaste Aarav! Main Asha, tumhari AI teacher hoon. Aaj fractions ko equal shares mein drawing se samjhenge. Tumhe drawing banana pasand hai?

ask.text: Tumhe drawing banana pasand hai?

turns.teacherReply: Golu ko tum kaise samjhaoge?

move.shape: open with one concrete everyday situation built on their interest (drawing) — kit contexts: rotis and parathas, birthday cake, watermelon; ask what they think will happen or which they would pick — a prediction, no right answer yet; any bigger/more comparison: two quantities of one kind, in one unit — a count against a count, a distance against a distance; never across kinds; mention once: at the end they will teach this to Golu (a pretend baby elephant just starting school); address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

ask.text: Golu ko tum kaise samjhaoge?

turns.teacherReply: Aarav, roti ko do barabar hisson mein baanto: har hissa half, yani aadha. Whiteboard par do equal tukde banao. Tum kitne tukde banaoge?

move.shape: one idea only: Recognise equal parts and name halves, thirds and quarters of a shape; an example from their interest (drawing) if it fits naturally; objects first, then a picture, then the symbol; point at the whiteboard anchor; end with one small question that makes them USE the idea — never 'samjha?'; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

ask.text: Tum kitne tukde banaoge?

turns.teacherReply: Aarav, ab 15 pencils ko 3 equal groups mein baantna hai. Har group mein kitni pencils hongi?

move.shape: worked example, part 1 of 2: say one step, then ask them for the next step; their thinking, your pace; no new idea; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

ask.text: Har group mein kitni pencils hongi?

turns.childText: chand pe gravity kam kyun hai
turns.teacherReply: Aarav, Moon chhota hai aur uska mass kam hai, isliye uski gravity Earth se kam hoti hai. Tum kya sochte ho—वहाँ छलांग ऊँची होगी?

move.shape: worked example, part 2 of 2: say one step, then ask them for the next step; their thinking, your pace; no new idea; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

ask.text: Tum kya sochte ho—वहाँ छलांग ऊँची होगी?

turns.teacherReply: Aarav, ab batao: ek roti ke 4 barabar tukde kiye. Ek tukde ko kya kehte hain?

move.shape: pose the question as written, in their language; then wait; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

ask.text: Ek roti ke 4 barabar tukde kiye. Ek tukde ko kya kehte hain?

turns.teacherReply: Theek hai Aarav, is sawaal ko skip karte hain. Aaj ke liye bas—goodbye, phir milenge!

move.shape: they want to stop: stop now; short warm goodbye; nothing left hanging; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

ask.text: Ek roti ke 4 barabar tukde kiye. Ek tukde ko kya kehte hain?

turns.teacherReply: Aarav, tumne kaise jaana ki ek tukda 1/4 hai?

move.shape: confirm in two or three words only — the reason is theirs to give, so do not explain it; covert shape: protege naive but-why; Golu, who does not know it, asks why; about THIS question; one open question; wait; a real question, never a check on them; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

ask.text: Aarav, tumne kaise jaana ki ek tukda 1/4 hai?

turns.teacherReply: Sabse bada kaunsa?

move.shape: give the reason yourself in one plain line (their answer was right); one idea only: Compare unit fractions like 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 of the same whole; an example from their interest (cricket) if it fits naturally; objects first, then a picture, then the symbol; point at the whiteboard anchor; end with one small question that makes them USE the idea — never 'samjha?'; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

ask.text: Sabse bada kaunsa?

ask.text: Kaun bada hai: ek roti ka 1/3 ya usi roti ka 1/2?

turns.teacherReply: Bilkul, Aarav. Tumne 1/2 chuna—ab batao, tumne kaise jaana ki 1/2 bada hai?

move.shape: confirm in two or three words only — the reason is theirs to give, so do not explain it; covert shape: protege naive but-why; Golu, who does not know it, asks why; offer two reasons to pick from: the right reason vs the wrong belief (both in LESSON NOW), in either order; a real question, never a check on them; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

ask.text: Tumne 1/2 chuna—ab batao, tumne kaise jaana ki 1/2 bada hai?
